title: Pure dimension
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. $X$ has *pure dimension $d$* (is *equidimensional of dimension $d$*) if every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ has Krull dimension [def-kun-dimension] $d$, the Krull dimension of a component being that of the topological space it is with the subspace topology (the supremum of the lengths $r$ of chains $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_r$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of it). The empty scheme has pure dimension $d$ for every $d$, having no irreducible components.

source.place: Definition 5.10.4, tag 0058 (definition-equidimensional), with the common dimension fixed to be $d$
